Magnetic Box MOQ and Cost Tiers: 2026 Pricing Guide for Buyers

Published August 19, 2026 · Buyer guide · By BestPackFactory

Quick answer

Expect magnetic box pricing in three bands: 500 pieces (USD 2.8-4.5 per unit), 1,000 pieces (USD 2.2-3.6) and 3,000 pieces (USD 1.8-2.9) for a mid-size 200 x 150 x 50 mm box with 2.0 mm greyboard and one foil area. Structure, magnet size, insert and finishes move the price more than quantity after 1,000 pieces. Request itemized quotes separating material, printing, insert, tooling and freight.

Why unit price falls with quantity

Two costs dominate: tooling and setup, which are fixed, and paper, magnets and labor, which scale. Going from 500 to 1,000 pieces usually cuts 15-25% off unit price because setup is amortized. Beyond 3,000 pieces the curve flattens to 5-10% per step, so mid-size brands rarely gain much by jumping from 3,000 to 5,000 unless they also consolidate SKUs.

What drives cost within one tier

At the same quantity, price moves with greyboard thickness (1.5 vs 2.5 mm), wrap paper grade (128 gsm art vs 157 gsm textured), magnet spec (2 x 10 mm vs 3 x 15 mm), insert complexity (flat paper tray vs flocked EVA with five cutouts) and finish count (one foil area vs foil plus emboss plus soft-touch). Changing any one of these can shift unit price by 10-20%.

How to compare quotes apples to apples

Ask every supplier for the same bill of materials: board thickness, wrap gsm, magnet size and pull, insert type, finish list and box exterior dimensions. Request tooling cost separately and whether it is reusable on reorders. Then compare delivered cost, not FOB alone: freight, duties and warehousing can add 15-30% for US or EU buyers.

2026 planning notes

Paperboard and magnet prices have been volatile, so request price validity in writing for 60-90 days and consider annual-volume agreements for predictable SKUs. Lock the dieline and finishes early; change requests after sample approval extend lead time by 3-7 days each and can push you past a launch date.

Buyer checklist

  1. Request quotes with an identical bill of materials across suppliers
  2. Separate tooling, unit price, insert and freight in the comparison
  3. Verify price validity in writing for 60-90 days
  4. Compare delivered (landed) cost, not FOB only
  5. Consolidate SKUs before quantity discounts are negotiated

Frequently asked questions

What is the cheapest magnetic box quantity that makes sense?

500 pieces per SKU is the practical floor for lid-and-base magnetic boxes; below that, setup cost dominates and per-unit price climbs steeply. If you need fewer, ask about mixed-SKU batches that share structure and printing.

How much does magnet size affect the price?

Magnet cost is small in absolute terms, roughly USD 0.02-0.10 per box depending on size, but upgrading from 2 x 10 mm to 3 x 15 mm can add 3-8% to unit price. It is usually worth paying for on heavy lids.

When do quantity discounts stop mattering?

After about 3,000 pieces the unit-price curve flattens to 5-10% per step. Larger orders still help lock paper pricing and freight rates, but structural choices (board, insert, finishes) matter more at that point.

What the Spec Means for Buyers

Magnetic box cost tiers follow board, magnet and finishing choices. Board tiers: 1200 gsm (1.8 mm) economy, 1500 gsm (2.2 mm) standard, 1800 gsm (2.8 mm) premium. Wrapping: 157 gsm C1S art paper is the baseline; 120 gsm specialty or kraft add texture. Magnet grade and position are confirmed from box size and flap geometry. Finishes from matte lamination (baseline) to soft-touch, hot foil, embossing and spot UV raise unit cost. All tiers run MOQ 500 PCS per size and artwork with corner gap ≤ 1.5 mm.

Frequently Asked Questions

What board tier should a premium brand choose?

1500–1800 gsm greyboard (2.2–2.8 mm) is the premium tier; 1200 gsm suits lighter, cost-driven projects.

What drives magnetic box cost most?

Board weight, wrapping paper, magnet specification and finishing complexity, in that order.
